steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Folding Attention Biases into Keys Makes Compacted KV Caches Run on Standard Kernels
summary: The method replaces the per-logit additive bias required by Attention Matching (AM) KV cache compaction by folding that bias into the kept keys along one closed-form direction per head, producing a plain cache that standard kernels such as FlashAttention and vLLM paged attention can serve without modification. The cost is a per-head fitting step on context queries plus one extra direction of storage, with output error bounded by how far each query's projection on that direction deviates from 1. It can fail when query projections vary widely from 1, and under published per-head budgets it no longer beats simply dropping the bias in KL divergence, with accuracy wins splitting evenly.
rationale: It removes the main deployment blocker for AM-style KV compaction on standard serving stacks, but the reader must first adopt AM compaction and validate that accuracy holds under their own per-head budgets, since the advantage over bias-dropping is not robust.
technique: Folding attention biases into keys for KV cache compaction

claims.statement: The method replaces the per-logit additive bias required by Attention Matching (AM) KV cache compaction by folding that bias into the kept keys along one closed-form direction per head, producing a plain cache that standard kernels such as FlashAttention and vLLM paged attention can serve without modification. The cost is a per-head fitting step on context queries plus one extra direction of storage, with output error bounded by how far each query's projection on that direction deviates from 1. It can fail when query projections vary widely from 1, and under published per-head budgets it no longer beats simply dropping the bias in KL divergence, with accuracy wins splitting evenly.

Folded caches served by unmodified vLLM matched Hugging Face answers on all 51 Qwen3-4B questions and greedy output on 180 of 200 Qwen3-14B LongBench samples, and were within noise of Attention Matching accuracy in 13 of 14 equal-budget settings; no speedup or memory-reduction factor over AM itself is claimed.
